hypotheses.justification: The proof only uses hcomm to show that (p' b₁, p'' b₁) is a compatible pair. It can be dropped, because hpb alone gives injectivity of b ↦ (p' b, p'' b). The pair (0,0) is compatible, since q' 0 = 0 = q'' 0. So hpb gives a unique b with p' b = 0 ∧ p'' b = 0, and b = 0 is such an element. Hence p' b = 0 ∧ p'' b = 0 implies b = 0. Now suppose p' b₁ = p' b₂ and p'' b₁ = p'' b₂. Then b₁ - b₂ satisfies p' (b₁ - b₂) = 0 and p'' (b₁ - b₂) = 0, because ring homomorphisms preserve subtraction. So b₁ - b₂ = 0, i.e. b₁ = b₂. This is a short replacement proof that does not mention hcomm. hcomm does not occur in the conclusion or in any other binder. The theorem stays true and provable without it, so it can be omitted with `omit hcomm in`.
